sentences.en: I recently looked up the number of women in Congress.
sentences.zh: 我最近查了一下国会中女性的人数。

sentences.en: Fewer than one in five legislators are women.
sentences.zh: 议员中女性不到五分之一。

sentences.en: At Fortune 500 companies, fewer than one in 20 CEOs are women.
sentences.zh: 在财富500强企业中，女性CEO不到二十分之一。

sentences.en: And look at all the presidents of the United States through Barack Obama.
sentences.zh: 看看奥巴马之前的所有美国总统。

sentences.en: Now, I know there was a long time when women couldn't be president,
sentences.zh: 我当然知道，过去很长一段时间女性都无法成为总统，

sentences.en: but if men and women had an equal shot at the White House,
sentences.zh: 但如果男女入主白宫的机会均等，

sentences.en: the odds of having 44 presidents in a row all be men?
sentences.zh: 连续44任总统全都是男性的概率是多少？

sentences.en: About one in 18 trillion.
sentences.zh: 大约十八万亿分之一。

sentences.en: What explains the dearth of women in top leadership positions?
sentences.zh: 是什么导致了高级领导层中女性的匮乏？

sentences.en: Is it bias?
sentences.zh: 是偏见吗？

sentences.en: A lack of role models?
sentences.zh: 缺乏榜样？

sentences.en: The old boys club?
sentences.zh: 老男孩俱乐部？

sentences.en: Sure, but it goes deeper than that.
sentences.zh: 当然有，但原因比这更深远。

sentences.en: Women are trapped in a catch-22,
sentences.zh: 女性陷入了两难的境地，

sentences.en: a paradox so deeply embedded in our culture that there are few means of escape.
sentences.zh: 这种悖论深深植根于我们的文化中，几乎无法摆脱。

sentences.en: And so it is really that very, very fine line
sentences.zh: 所以这真的是一条非常、非常微妙的界线，

sentences.en: between being a shrew on the one hand and a puppet on the other
sentences.zh: 一面是尖酸刻薄的悍妇，另一面是任人摆布的傀儡，

sentences.en: that any woman in public life has to walk.
sentences.zh: 任何参与公众生活的女性都必须走过这条钢丝。

sentences.en: The puppet, the shrew, and the double bind facing women who want to lead.
sentences.zh: 傀儡、悍妇，以及想要领导地位的女性所面临的双重困境。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: A few years ago, one of our listeners decided to switch careers.
sentences.zh: 几年前，我们的一位听众决定转换职业。

sentences.en: So my name is Debra Mehta,
sentences.zh: 我叫黛布拉·梅塔，

sentences.en: and I am a second-year marketing student in an MBA program.
sentences.zh: 我是MBA项目的一名二年级市场营销专业学生。

sentences.en: Debra had been a successful teacher,
sentences.zh: 黛布拉曾经是一名成功的教师，

sentences.en: but the business world appealed to her.
sentences.zh: 但商界对她很有吸引力。

sentences.en: She thought she would be a good fit.
sentences.zh: 她觉得自己很适合。

sentences.en: So did the program to which she applied.
sentences.zh: 她申请的项目也是这么认为的。

sentences.en: She was awarded a full scholarship.
sentences.zh: 她获得了全额奖学金。

sentences.en: Soon, she was sharing the good news with an old friend.
sentences.zh: 很快，她就把这个好消息分享给了一位老朋友。

sentences.en: We met for coffee one day, and she is very nice.
sentences.zh: 有一天我们见面喝咖啡，她人非常好。

sentences.en: I'm still really good friends with her.
sentences.zh: 我和她至今仍是很好的朋友。

sentences.en: But she said to me,
sentences.zh: 但她对我说，

sentences.en: I really can't see you in business.
sentences.zh: 我真的觉得你不适合经商。

sentences.en: I think you're, you know, too sweet for the business world.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你，你知道的，对商界来说太天真了。

sentences.en: It was the beginning of a series of comments
sentences.zh: 这是一系列言论的开始，

sentences.en: that undermined her belief that she could be a leader or a manager.
sentences.zh: 这些言论削弱了她认为自己能成为领导者或管理者的信念。

sentences.en: Later that year, Debra's voice was the problem,
sentences.zh: 那年晚些时候，黛布拉的声音成了问题，

sentences.en: specifically her habit of ending sentences on a higher pitch.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，是她习惯在句尾时语调上扬。

sentences.en: A professor during a class mentioned that I do that,
sentences.zh: 课堂上有一位教授提到我这样做，

sentences.en: that I raise my, you know, pitch at the end of a sentence.
sentences.zh: 也就是说我会在句尾提高语调。

sentences.en: The implication was that Debra sounded like a lightweight,
sentences.zh: 这暗示着黛布拉听起来像个无足轻重的人，

sentences.en: not manager material.
sentences.zh: 不是管理者的料。

sentences.en: Debra says she wasn't prepared for the offhand remarks.
sentences.zh: 黛布拉说她对这些随口说出的话毫无准备。

sentences.en: I mean, it really was leading me to lose confidence.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这真的让我失去了信心。

sentences.en: The criticism of my voice,
sentences.zh: 对我声音的批评，

sentences.en: and then, you know, everyone, not everyone,
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，每个人，也不是每个人，

sentences.en: but several people telling me, you know,
sentences.zh: 但有几个人告诉我，你知道的，

sentences.en: I'm too sweet for business.
sentences.zh: 我对于经商来说太温顺了。

sentences.en: I think it really, it really affected me.
sentences.zh: 我想这真的、真的对我产生了影响。

sentences.en: This is one side of the Catch-22.
sentences.zh: 这就是双重困境的一面。

sentences.en: Women like Debra are seen as not tough enough to be leaders.
sentences.zh: 像黛布拉这样的女性被认为不够强硬，无法成为领导者。

sentences.en: Another listener, Thule Winson, made a different set of choices.
sentences.zh: 另一位听众图利·温森做出了不同的选择。

sentences.en: As a manager at a construction company,
sentences.zh: 作为一家建筑公司的经理，

sentences.en: a female leader in a man's world,
sentences.zh: 在男人的世界里作为一名女性领导者，

sentences.en: she decided to be strategic.
sentences.zh: 她决定采取战略性的做法。

sentences.en: From the way she dresses,
sentences.zh: 从她的穿着打扮来看，

sentences.en: I've definitely chosen to go a more masculine path,
sentences.zh: 我确实选择了一条更男孩子气的路线，

sentences.en: wearing Oxford shoes and button-downs
sentences.zh: 穿着牛津鞋、系扣衬衫，

sentences.en: and straight pulled-back hair and pants.
sentences.zh: 梳着笔直的背头，穿着裤子。

sentences.en: To the way she greets clients.
sentences.zh: 到她迎接客户的方式。

sentences.en: You just, you know, just go in there and grab that hand
sentences.zh: 你只需要，你知道的，走进去握住那只手，

sentences.en: and squeeze it because you have muscles too.
sentences.zh: 用力捏紧，因为你也有肌肉。

sentences.en: I think that tends to help them go,
sentences.zh: 我觉得这往往有助于让他们觉得，

sentences.en: oh, wow, this is not just a lady.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇，这可不仅仅是一位女士。

sentences.en: Thule doesn't want to appear soft or overly feminine
sentences.zh: 图利不想显得柔弱或过于女性化，

sentences.en: because she knows that would be seen as weakness.
sentences.zh: 因为她知道那会被视为软弱。

sentences.en: But appearing tough turns out to create its own set of probleMs.
sentences.zh: 但表现得强硬结果却带来了它自己的一系列问题。

sentences.en: It's definitely a double-edged sword
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一把双刃剑，

sentences.en: because if I'm outspoken,
sentences.zh: 因为如果我直言不讳，

sentences.en: all of a sudden the men in the office will joke about,
sentences.zh: 办公室里的男人们突然就会开玩笑说，

sentences.en: oh, whoa, whoa, watch out for Thule.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇，哇，小心图利。

sentences.en: Watch out.
sentences.zh: 小心点。

sentences.en: She's dangerous, that one.
sentences.zh: 她很危险，那个女人。

sentences.en: Dangerous.
sentences.zh: 很危险。

sentences.en: Not driven.
sentences.zh: 不是有进取心。

sentences.en: Not strong.
sentences.zh: 不是坚强。

sentences.en: Dangerous.
sentences.zh: 而是危险。

sentences.en: We tell you their stories because together,
sentences.zh: 我们把他们的故事讲给你们听，因为把这些放在一起，

sentences.en: Thule and Debra's experiences
sentences.zh: 图利和黛布拉的经历

sentences.en: reveal a powerful phenomenon
sentences.zh: 揭示了一种强有力的现象，

sentences.en: that plays out when women strive to become leaders.
sentences.zh: 当女性努力成为领导者时，这种现象就会上演。

sentences.en: The problem doesn't end with getting to the corner office.
sentences.zh: 问题并不会随着进入高管办公室而结束。

sentences.en: Women confront the same issues
sentences.zh: 女性在行使权力时

sentences.en: when it comes to exercising power.
sentences.zh: 同样面临这些问题。

sentences.en: It's a double bind.
sentences.zh: 这就是双重困境。

sentences.en: Social psychologist Alice Eggly says
sentences.zh: 社会心理学家爱丽丝·埃格利表示，

sentences.en: the double bind comes about
sentences.zh: 双重困境的出现

sentences.en: because of a series of unconscious,
sentences.zh: 是因为我们有一系列无意识的、

sentences.en: interlocking stereotypes we have
sentences.zh: 相互交织的刻板印象，

sentences.en: about men, women, and the nature of leadership.
sentences.zh: 这些印象关乎男性、女性以及领导力的本质。

sentences.en: The female gender role, you know,
sentences.zh: 女性的性别角色，你知道的，

sentences.en: is based on the stereotype that women are nice and kind
sentences.zh: 是基于女性应当友善、亲切和富有同情心的刻板印象，但这同时也是一种期待。

sentences.en: and compassionate, but it's also expected.
sentences.zh: 所以人们期望女性要表现得随和、友好

sentences.en: So people expect women to be kind of nice and friendly
sentences.zh: 并且面带微笑。

sentences.en: and smile.
sentences.zh: 现在，爱丽丝说，想想我们对领导者的文化刻板印象。

sentences.en: Now, says Alice, consider our cultural stereotype about leaders.
sentences.zh: 在领导岗位上，人们期望你能够掌权，

sentences.en: In a leadership role, one is expected to take charge
sentences.zh: 并且至少在某些时候，

sentences.en: and sometimes, at least,
sentences.zh: 要表现出强硬，做出艰难的决定，

sentences.en: to demonstrate toughness, make tough decisions,
sentences.zh: 在推动组织前进时表现得非常果断，

sentences.en: be very assertive in bringing an organization forward,
sentences.zh: 有时甚至要以正当理由解雇员工等。

sentences.en: sometimes fire people for cause, etc.
sentences.zh: 所以女人该怎么做呢？

sentences.en: So what's a woman to do?
sentences.zh: 是做一个温和、亲切、友好的人，

sentences.en: Be nice and kind and friendly,
sentences.zh: 正如我们对女性的性别刻板印象所要求的那样，

sentences.en: as our gender stereotypes about women require,
sentences.zh: 还是做一个强硬、果断的人，

sentences.en: or be tough and decisive,
sentences.zh: 正如我们对领导力的刻板印象所要求的那样？

sentences.en: as our stereotypes about leadership demand?
sentences.zh: 成为前者就会被视为亲切但软弱。

sentences.en: To be one is to be seen as nice, but weak.
sentences.zh: 成为后者就会被视为能干但讨人嫌。

sentences.en: To be the other is to be seen as competent, but unlikable.
sentences.zh: 双重困境不仅存在于商界的图利和黛布拉这样的女性身上，

sentences.en: The double bind exists for women like Thule and Deborah
sentences.zh: 也存在于公众生活中，

sentences.en: in the business world,
sentences.zh: 甚至对那些拥有巨大权力和经验的女性来说也是如此。

sentences.en: but it also exists in public life,
sentences.zh: 我们采访了两位当选高级公职的女性。

sentences.en: even for women with enormous power and experience.
sentences.zh: 一位是民主党人，另一位是共和党人。

sentences.en: We talked to two women elected to high office.
sentences.zh: 她们的故事有许多相似之处。

sentences.en: One is a Democrat, the other is a Republican.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，你们可能会注意到我们称呼嘉宾

sentences.en: Their stories have many similarities.
sentences.zh: 时用的是她们的名。

sentences.en: By the way, you may notice we refer to our guests
sentences.zh: 媒体在指代人名时存在性别偏见。

sentences.en: by their first names.
sentences.zh: 记者通常用女性的名来称呼她们，

sentences.en: There are gender biases in the way the media use names.
sentences.zh: 而用男性的姓来称呼他们。

sentences.en: Journalists regularly refer to women by their first names
sentences.zh: 在这个播客中，为了保持对话的轻松感，

sentences.en: and men by their last names.
sentences.zh: 我们对所有嘉宾都直呼其名。

sentences.en: On this podcast, in the interest of being conversational,
sentences.zh: 当卡罗尔·莫斯利·布劳恩当选美国参议员时，

sentences.en: we use first names for all guests.
sentences.zh: 她取得了突破性的历史成就。

sentences.en: When Carol Mosley Braun was elected to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 她是第一位非洲裔女性参议员。

sentences.en: Senate,
sentences.zh: 卡罗尔说在成长过程中，

sentences.en: she achieved a powerful firSt.
sentences.zh: 她的父母保护她不让她发现

sentences.en: She was the first female African-American senator.
sentences.zh: 偏见是如何限制她的选择的。

sentences.en: Carol says growing up,
sentences.zh: 我的父母从未向我灌输过这样的观念，

sentences.en: her parents shielded her from finding out
sentences.zh: 即我的种族或性别在任何方面限制了我，

sentences.en: how bias might limit her choices.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得，你知道的，只要我想做并且能做，

sentences.en: My parents had never given me a notion
sentences.zh: 无论什么事我都可以去做。

sentences.en: that I was limited in any way by my race or my gender,
sentences.zh: 但当她进入政坛后，

sentences.en: and that, you know, I could just do whatever it was
sentences.zh: 卡罗尔意识到种族和性别确实很重要。

sentences.en: that I thought I wanted to do and could do.
sentences.zh: 在这两者中，她曾认为种族主义会是更大的障碍。

sentences.en: But when she got into politics,
sentences.zh: 我必须告诉你们，我认为在某些方面，

sentences.en: Carol realized that race and gender did matter.
sentences.zh: 性别偏见比种族偏见

sentences.en: Of the two, she thought that racism would be the bigger barrier.
sentences.zh: 更为深远，也更触及我们文化的核心。

sentences.en: And I have to tell you that I think in some regards
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这才是令人惊讶的地方。

sentences.en: the gender biases are more profound
sentences.zh: 我预料到会因为种族或性别而受到一些阻力。

sentences.en: and more central to our culture than even the racial ones.
sentences.zh: 我没有料到的是，来自性别的阻力

sentences.en: And that, for me, was the surprise.
sentences.zh: 会如此显著，

sentences.en: I was expecting some pushback based on race and or gender.
sentences.zh: 甚至比种族的阻力还要大。

sentences.en: What I wasn't expecting was that the gender pushback
sentences.zh: 但就在卡罗尔赢得竞选后不久，

sentences.en: would be as pronounced as it was,
sentences.zh: 她说她面临了第二个陷阱，

sentences.en: even more so than the racial ones.
sentences.zh: 也就是双重困境的另一面。

sentences.en: But shortly after Carol won her race,
sentences.zh: 有一次，她在参议院大厅里发表了慷慨激昂的呼吁，

sentences.en: she says she confronted a second trap,
sentences.zh: 但她觉得同事们根本没在听她讲话。

sentences.en: the other side of the double bind.
sentences.zh: 而摆脱这种安全网正是所谓福利改革的全部意义所在。

sentences.en: One time, she made an impassioned plea on the floor of the Senate,
sentences.zh: 但她觉得同事们根本没在听她讲话。

sentences.en: but she felt her colleagues were just tuning her out.
sentences.zh: 而摆脱这种安全网正是所谓福利改革的全部意义所在。

sentences.en: And getting rid of that safety net is what this so-called welfare reform is all about.
sentences.zh: 而摆脱这种安全网正是所谓福利改革的全部意义所在。

sentences.en: All they could hear was a shrill black woman.
sentences.zh: 他们能听到的只有一个声音尖锐的黑人女性。

sentences.en: I came home that night, I was so upset and demeaned, to use the word,
sentences.zh: 那天我回到家，感到非常沮丧和受辱，如果用这个词的话，

sentences.en: that I thought, OK, that's it.
sentences.zh: 以至于我想，好吧，就这样吧。

sentences.en: I can't take this anymore.
sentences.zh: 我再也无法忍受了。

sentences.en: I'm going to quit.
sentences.zh: 我要辞职。

sentences.en: She didn't quit.
sentences.zh: 她没有辞职。

sentences.en: But Carol still vividly recalls how unfair it felt.
sentences.zh: 但卡罗尔依然清晰地记得那种不公平的感觉。

sentences.en: And it wasn't just over how she was being treated.
sentences.zh: 而且这不仅仅是因为她受到的对待。

sentences.en: She saw her experience in the long light of history.
sentences.zh: 她从历史的长河中看到了自己的遭遇。

sentences.en: In the 15th century, women who talked back,
sentences.zh: 在15世纪，那些顶嘴的女性，

sentences.en: they would put weights on their tongue and make them walk around the square.
sentences.zh: 人们会在她们的舌头上挂上重物，让她们在广场上游行。

sentences.en: That was a shrew's punishment,
sentences.zh: 那是对悍妇的惩罚，

sentences.en: the idea being that you're not supposed to have opinions about things outside of the home.
sentences.zh: 其核心观念是，你本不该对家门之外的事情有任何意见。

sentences.en: And so that's a real danger for any woman in public life.
sentences.zh: 因此，这对任何身处公众视线中的女性来说都是一种真正的危险。

sentences.en: So every stranger gets to comment on what they think about you
sentences.zh: 所以每一个陌生人都可以对他们关于你的看法评头论足，

sentences.en: and what they think about what you just said.
sentences.zh: 以及对你刚刚说的话发表意见。

sentences.en: And if you said too much, that becomes a danger.
sentences.zh: 如果你说得太多，那就成了一种危险。

sentences.en: If you said too little, that's a danger also.
sentences.zh: 如果你说得太少，同样也是一种危险。

sentences.en: And so it is really that very, very fine line
sentences.zh: 所以这真的是一条非常非常微妙的界限，

sentences.en: between being a shrew on the one hand and a puppet on the other
sentences.zh: 一方面是悍妇，另一方面是提线木偶，

sentences.en: that any woman in public life has to walk.
sentences.zh: 任何在公众生活中抛头露面的女性都必须小心走好这条钢丝。

sentences.en: After serving one term in the Senate,
sentences.zh: 在参议院任职一届后，

sentences.en: Carol lost re-election in 1998.
sentences.zh: 卡罗尔在1998年的连任竞选中落败。

sentences.en: There is a sense that a woman has to be gracious and civil and smart and smile.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种观念，认为女性必须亲切、文明、聪明而且面带微笑。

sentences.en: This is Connie Morella.
sentences.zh: 这是康妮·莫雷拉。

sentences.en: Connie served for 16 years as a Republican congresswoman from Maryland.
sentences.zh: 康妮曾担任马里兰州的共和党女众议员长达16年。

sentences.en: But she's got to be strong also and indicate that she's going to persevere.
sentences.zh: 但她同时也必须坚强，表现出她会坚持到底的决心。

sentences.en: Like Democrat Carol Mosley Braun, Connie says at times she struggled to be heard.
sentences.zh: 和民主党人卡罗尔·莫斯利·布朗一样，康妮说她有时很难发出自己的声音。

sentences.en: In a committee room, when I wasn't chair of the committee,
sentences.zh: 在委员会会议室里，当我不是委员会主席时，

sentences.en: I would respond to a question or a comment on an issue.
sentences.zh: 我会回应关于某个议题的问题或评论。

sentences.en: And I would say, well, thank you, Connie.
sentences.zh: 然后我会说，嗯，谢谢你，康妮。

sentences.en: That's great.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: And then a little later, Representative Smith said the very same thing I did.
sentences.zh: 然后过了一会儿，史密斯众议员说了跟我完全一样的话。

sentences.en: And it was, oh, Congressman Smith, that was fabulous.
sentences.zh: 接着大家就会说，哦，史密斯议员，这太了不起了。

sentences.en: Let the record show that you have accomplished that or whatever.
sentences.zh: 请记录在案，你已经取得了这一成就，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And I think, gee, I just said that.
sentences.zh: 而我想，天哪，我刚刚才说过这话。

sentences.en: Connie Morella, Carol Mosley Braun, Tule Winson, Deborah Mehta.
sentences.zh: 康妮·莫雷拉、卡罗尔·莫斯利·布朗、图利·温森、黛博拉·梅塔。

sentences.en: All these women feel they've experienced bias.
sentences.zh: 所有这些女性都觉得她们经历过偏见。

sentences.en: But here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 但关键是：

sentences.en: How do we know, scientifically, that they're right?
sentences.zh: 我们如何用科学的方法证明她们是对的？

sentences.en: Carol Mosley Braun's Senate colleagues may have felt their perception of her was accurate.
sentences.zh: 卡罗尔·莫斯利·布朗在参议院的同僚们可能觉得他们对她的看法是准确的。

sentences.en: The newspaper cartoonist may have felt she really was easily manipulated.
sentences.zh: 报纸漫画家可能觉得她确实很容易被操纵。

sentences.en: In fact, Carol herself, in her interview with us, listed numerous missteps she'd made as a campaigner and as a senator.
sentences.zh: 事实上，卡罗尔本人在接受我们采访时，也列举了她在竞选和担任参议员期间犯下的无数失误。

sentences.en: How can we tell with scientific certainty whether Carol was the victim of bias?
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能以科学的确定性来判断卡罗尔是否是偏见的受害者？

sentences.en: When we look at a woman leader who appears incompetent or shrill, how do we know if we're seeing reality or just seeing the world through the lens of our own unconscious biases?
sentences.zh: 当我们看到一个看起来无能或声音尖锐的女领导时，我们怎么知道我们看到的是现实，还是仅仅通过我们自己无意识偏见的有色眼镜来看世界？

sentences.en: This is where laboratory experiments are essential.
sentences.zh: 这就是实验室实验至关重要的地方。

sentences.en: They allow us to see precisely what's happening.
sentences.zh: 它们让我们能够精确地看到正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: We keep everything identical.
sentences.zh: 我们保持一切完全相同。

sentences.en: We expose people to the various, what we call, experimental conditions.
sentences.zh: 我们让人们接触各种我们所谓的实验条件。

sentences.en: And at the end of the day, if we find a difference, we can say that it has to be due to that thing that we were studying.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，如果我们发现了差异，我们就可以说这必定是由我们正在研究的那项因素引起的。

sentences.en: And that's the nature of a controlled experiment.
sentences.zh: 这就是对照实验的本质。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: When we judge a person's character, we usually think our opinions are based on fact.
sentences.zh: 当我们判断一个人的品格时，我们通常认为自己的观点是基于事实的。

sentences.en: What we forget is that the world that enters our brain has been filtered.
sentences.zh: 我们忘记的是，进入我们大脑的世界已经被过滤过了。

sentences.en: Figuring out what those filters are and how they distort our vision has long intrigued Madeleine Heilman.
sentences.zh: 找出这些过滤器是什么以及它们如何扭曲我们的视线，长期以来一直深深吸引着玛德琳·海尔曼。

sentences.en: She's a psychology professor at New York University who focuses on gender stereotypes and bias, particularly when it comes to leadership.
sentences.zh: 她是纽约大学的一位心理学教授，专注于研究性别刻板印象和偏见，特别是涉及领导力方面的偏见。

sentences.en: What we have found consistently is that when we present women and men with exactly the same credentials, qualifications, and backgrounds
sentences.zh: 我们始终发现的是，当我们向女性和男性提供完全相同的资历、资格和背景时，

sentences.en: for a job that is traditionally male, held by men in our culture, thought to require male attributes,
sentences.zh: 为了一个传统上由男性担任、我们文化中由男性把持、被认为需要男性特质的工作，

sentences.en: we consistently find that the woman is seen as more incompetent than the man.
sentences.zh: 我们始终发现女性被认为比男性更加无能。

sentences.en: The problem doesn't end there.
sentences.zh: 问题并没有到此为止。

sentences.en: Sometimes women really do show their competence, and it's unavoidable, and we can't deny it.
sentences.zh: 有时候女性确实展现了她们的能力，这是不可避免的，我们无法否认。

sentences.en: And what happens then?
sentences.zh: 那接下来会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, the research that I've done has shown that when women are truly successful in areas where they're not expected to be,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我做过的研究表明，当女性在不被期望取得成功的领域真正取得成功时，

sentences.en: there's a very negative reaction.
sentences.zh: 会出现非常负面的反应。

sentences.en: There's disapproval, and they are penalized.
sentences.zh: 会有不赞同的声音，她们会受到惩罚。

sentences.en: They are disliked, but they're also seen as really, almost really awful depictions of what kinds of people they are.
sentences.zh: 她们不受欢迎，而且被视为她们这类人极其糟糕的写照。

sentences.en: Words like bitter, and quarrelsome, and selfish, and deceitful, and devious, and manipulative, and cold.
sentences.zh: 诸如痛苦、好争吵、自私、虚伪、狡猾、爱操纵和冷酷之类的词汇。

sentences.en: These are words that are attributed to these women who are successful where they are not supposed to be,
sentences.zh: 这些词都被归咎于那些在不该成功的领域取得成功的女性，

sentences.en: and I put that in quotes.
sentences.zh: 我这里把这话加上引号。

sentences.en: We have terms for these people, you know, Ice Queen, and Dragon Lady, and Iron Maiden, and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 我们对这样的人有各种称呼，你知道的，冰雪女王、龙夫人、铁娘子，等等等等。

sentences.en: I want to emphasize these aren't Madeleine's opinions.
sentences.zh: 我想强调，这些不是玛德琳个人的观点。

sentences.en: They are the findings of her experiments.
sentences.zh: 它们是她实验的结果。

sentences.en: In one study, Madeleine asked volunteers to evaluate a high-powered manager joining a company.
sentences.zh: 在一项研究中，玛德琳让志愿者评估一位即将加入公司的强势经理。

sentences.en: Sometimes, volunteers are told the manager is a man.
sentences.zh: 有时，志愿者被告知这位经理是个男士。

sentences.en: Other times, they're told it's a woman.
sentences.zh: 其他时候，他们被告知是个女士。

sentences.en: When the person was presented as a very high-power person who was very ambitious,
sentences.zh: 当这个人被表现为一个非常有权势且极具雄心的人时，

sentences.en: we found that the person was seen as much more unlikable when it was a woman than when it was a man.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，如果是个女性，人们会觉得她比是个男性时更加讨人厌。

sentences.en: To be clear, the high-powered male and female manager are described in identical terms, down to the letter.
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，这位强势的男经理和女经理的描述在字面上是完全相同的。

sentences.en: The only thing different is that one is said to be a man, and the other is said to be a woman.
sentences.zh: 唯一的区别在于一个被说成是男性，另一个被说成是女性。

sentences.en: Madeleine has also looked at what happens when someone joins a company, but is not said to be in a position of power.
sentences.zh: 玛德琳还研究了当某人加入公司但并未处于权势地位时会发生什么。

sentences.en: If we didn't give information about how successful the person was, just had them applying for a job,
sentences.zh: 如果我们不透露这个人的成功程度，只是让他们申请一份工作，

sentences.en: we find that the women are as likable as the man, but they're seen as less competent.
sentences.zh: 我们发现女性和男性一样讨人喜欢，但她们被认为能力较低。

sentences.en: And that is the rock and the hard place, the double bind, that if it's not clear that you're successful
sentences.zh: 这就是左右为难的困境，也就是双重束缚：如果不清楚你是否成功，

sentences.en: and you have the same information about a woman and a man, the woman is seen as less competent.
sentences.zh: 而你对女性和男性拥有相同的信息，女性就会被认为能力较差。

sentences.en: If you have very clear indication that there is success, then the woman is rated as unlikable.
sentences.zh: 如果你有非常明确的迹象表明其获得了成功，那么这位女性就会被评为不讨人喜欢。

sentences.en: They see her as competent, but unlikable.
sentences.zh: 他们认为她有能力，但很不讨喜。

sentences.en: Madeleine says the double bind arises because our minds are trying to align our stereotypes about men and women
sentences.zh: 玛德琳说，双重束缚的产生是因为我们的大脑试图将我们对男女的刻板印象

sentences.en: with our stereotypes about leadership.
sentences.zh: 与我们对领导力的刻板印象相调和。

sentences.en: We have conceptions of these jobs and these positions and what is required to do them well.
sentences.zh: 我们对这些工作、这些职位以及做好它们所需要的要求有特定的概念。

sentences.en: And there's a lack of fit between how we see women and what these positions require.
sentences.zh: 我们对女性的看法与这些职位所要求的能力之间存在着不匹配。

sentences.en: The biases Madeleine describes aren't just held by men.
sentences.zh: 玛德琳所描述的偏见不仅仅存在于男性之中。

sentences.en: They're held by both sexes, which explains why many female leaders
sentences.zh: 男女两性都存在这种偏见，这就解释了为什么许多女性领导者

sentences.en: encounter derision and suspicion from both men and women.
sentences.zh: 会同时遭到男性和女性的嘲笑与怀疑。

sentences.en: I think that this comes from the social roles that people have played over time.
sentences.zh: 我认为这源于人们随着时间推移所扮演的社会角色。

sentences.en: Women stayed home and they took care.
sentences.zh: 女性呆在家里照顾家庭。

sentences.en: Men went out and they took, you know, they took charge of things.
sentences.zh: 男性则走出去，你知道的，他们掌控大局。

sentences.en: That is the kind of origin, I think, of the stereotypes that we hold.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是我们所持有的刻板印象的起源。

sentences.en: We have very strong feelings about how men and women are.
sentences.zh: 我们对男性的行事方式和女性的行事方式有着非常强烈的看法。

sentences.en: And that leads to the idea that women are less competent than men in a lot of these fields that we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 这就导致了一种观点，即在我们讨论的许多领域中，女性的能力不如男性。

sentences.en: And we have real strong ideas about how they should be.
sentences.zh: 而且我们对她们应该是什么样有着非常强烈的想法。

sentences.en: And that leads to this dislike when they go over the line, when they tread where they're not supposed to be.
sentences.zh: 这就导致了当她们越过界限、涉足本不该她们涉足的领域时，人们就会产生这种反感。

sentences.en: There are other aspects to the double bind.
sentences.zh: 双重束缚还有其他方面。

sentences.en: Female leaders can get in trouble for displaying emotion, but also for not displaying emotion.
sentences.zh: 女性领导者可能会因为表现出情绪而陷入麻烦，但也会因为没有表现出情绪而惹上麻烦。

sentences.en: Lisa Feldman Barrett is a psychology professor at Northeastern University
sentences.zh: 莉萨·费尔德曼·巴雷特是东北大学的心理学教授，

sentences.en: and author of the book, How Emotions Are Made.
sentences.zh: 也是《情绪是如何产生的》一书的作者。

sentences.en: There's an implication that if a woman expresses emotion, that she's either unsuitable for leadership or unstable in some way.
sentences.zh: 这里有一种暗示，即如果女性表达情绪，要么说明她不适合担任领导职务，要么说明她在某种程度上不稳定。

sentences.en: Or if she doesn't express enough emotion, she's also seen, rather than being seen as rational and kind of level-headed,
sentences.zh: 或者如果她表达的情绪不够，人们也不会认为她理性、头脑冷静，

sentences.en: she's seen as, you know, not empathic, not warm, and generally not trustworthy.
sentences.zh: 反而会觉得她，你知道的，缺乏同理心、不够温暖，总体上不值得信任。

sentences.en: In one experiment, Lisa showed volunteers pictures of faces and asked why the subject was expressing an emotion.
sentences.zh: 在一个实验中，莉萨向志愿者展示了面部照片，并询问为什么照片中的人会表现出某种情绪。

sentences.en: She found that the volunteers thought men's emotions were shaped by what was going on around them,
sentences.zh: 她发现志愿者认为男性的情绪是由他们周围发生的事情决定的，

sentences.en: but that women's emotions were shaped by their nature.
sentences.zh: 但女性的情绪是由她们的本性决定的。

sentences.en: Both men and women, when they were looking at female faces expressing emotion,
sentences.zh: 无论是男性还是女性，当他们看着表达情绪的女性面孔时，

sentences.en: believed that this was caused by a woman's emotional nature.
sentences.zh: 都认为这是由女性的情绪化本性引起的。

sentences.en: She's just a neurotic person, she's just unstable, she's just untrustworthy.
sentences.zh: 她就是个神经质的人，她就是不稳定，她就是不值得信任。

sentences.en: As opposed to when they were looking at male faces expressing emotion,
sentences.zh: 与此相反，当他们看着表达情绪的男性面孔时，

sentences.en: they were more likely to say, oh, he's just having a bad day, something bad happened to him.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能说，哦，他只是碰巧今天倒霉，他身上发生了不好的事。

sentences.en: Lots of people have suggested ways out of the double bind.
sentences.zh: 许多人提出了摆脱双重束缚的方法。

sentences.en: Some say women should ignore criticisms about incompetence and plunge full steam ahead.
sentences.zh: 有人说女性应该忽视对她们无能的批评，全速前进。

sentences.en: If they then appear unlikable, they should also go out of their way to demonstrate kindness
sentences.zh: 如果她们随后显得不讨人喜欢，她们也应该竭尽全力表现出善良，

sentences.en: in order to keep people from seeing them as competent but cold.
sentences.zh: 以免人们把她们看作是有能力但冷酷无情的人。

sentences.en: There is something disturbing about these ideas.
sentences.zh: 这些想法有些令人不安。

sentences.en: They ask women, who are the victims here, to compensate for the biases of others.
sentences.zh: 它们要求身受其害的女性去弥补他人的偏见。

sentences.en: Many experts also think that as society changes, our stereotypes will change as well.
sentences.zh: 许多专家还认为，随着社会的改变，我们的刻板印象也会随之改变。

sentences.en: If more women make it through the labyrinth and get to the top,
sentences.zh: 如果有更多的女性穿过迷宫并登上顶峰，

sentences.en: fewer people will have trouble seeing women as leaders.
sentences.zh: 就会有越少的人在把女性视为领导者时感到困难。

sentences.en: Many countries and organizations are coming to think of leadership as being collaborative
sentences.zh: 许多国家和组织开始将领导力视为一种协作关系，

sentences.en: rather than dictatorial.
sentences.zh: 而不是专制独裁。

sentences.en: The less we think of leaders as alpha males,
sentences.zh: 我们越是不把领导者视为阿尔法男性，

sentences.en: the easier it's going to be for our unconscious minds to see women as leaders.
sentences.zh: 我们的无意识大脑就越容易将女性视为领导者。

sentences.en: If there's one common thread here, it's that ending the double bind can't be just on the women
sentences.zh: 如果说这里有一个共同的主线，那就是打破双重束缚不能只靠那些

sentences.en: reaching for high office or the corner office.
sentences.zh: 争取高位或核心职位的女性。

sentences.en: It has to be on all of us.
sentences.zh: 这必须依靠我们所有人。

sentences.en: This week's episode of Hidden Brain was produced by Jenny Schmidt and edited by Tara Boyle.
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》由珍妮·施密特制作，塔拉·博伊尔编辑。

sentences.en: Our staff also includes Maggie Penman and Renee Klar.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作人员还包括玛吉·彭曼和蕾妮·克拉尔。

sentences.en: If you like this episode, I'm going to ask that you tell two friends,
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这一集，我希望你能把这个节目推荐给两个朋友，

sentences.en: one man and one woman, about the show.
sentences.zh: 一个男的，一个女的。

sentences.en: Our unsung hero this week is Anya Grunman.
sentences.zh: 我们本周的无名英雄是阿尼亚·格伦曼。

sentences.en: She's the person who oversees NPR's podcasts.
sentences.zh: 她是负责监督NPR播客的人。

sentences.en: She's always had our back, and there's a reason her calendar is always maxed out.
sentences.zh: 她一直都是我们的坚强后盾，她的日程总是排得满满的，这是有原因的。

sentences.en: Anya is the very definition of that collaborative leader we were just talking about.
sentences.zh: 阿尼亚正是我们刚才谈到的那种协作型领导的完美定义。

sentences.en: She makes everyone around her better.
sentences.zh: 她让身边的每一个人都变得更好。

sentences.en: Today we're also honoring the work of another remarkable colleague,
sentences.zh: 今天我们还要表彰另一位杰出同事的工作，

sentences.en: producer Chris Benderev, who's been with us at Hidden Brain for a few months.
sentences.zh: 制作人克里斯·本德雷夫，他在《隐藏的大脑》和我们一起工作了几个月。

sentences.en: He's about to return to his role on NPR's Embedded podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 他即将回到NPR的《内幕》播客担任他的职务。

sentences.en: Chris is great at everything he does, which would be a little obnoxious
sentences.zh: 克里斯做什么都很优秀，如果不是因为他同时也是我们认识的最好的人之一，

sentences.en: if he weren't also one of the nicest people we know.
sentences.zh: 这可能会显得有点讨人厌。

sentences.en: Thank you, Chris, for all the great work you've done on this show.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，克里斯，感谢你为这个节目所做的一切出色工作。

sentences.en: You can find more Hidden Brain on Facebook and Twitter,
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook和Twitter上找到更多关于《隐藏的大脑》的内容，

sentences.en: and listen for my stories on your local public radio station.
sentences.zh: 也可以在当地的公共广播电台上收听我的故事。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vethantham, and this is NPR.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹坦，这里是NPR。
